clue.text: Charm will ensure entry!

definitions.meaning: to charm someone is to delight or enchant them, a verb stressed on the second syllable
a way in, such as a door or gate

explanation.surface: A doorman says charm alone will get you past the velvet rope.
explanation.definitionFit: One spelling serves both the verb meaning to enchant and the noun for a doorway or way in.

clue.text: Tax being cut

definitions.meaning: a duty charged on goods produced or sold at home
to cut out, as a surgeon removes tissue

explanation.surface: A levy that is being trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: One spelling covers a home duty on goods and the verb meaning to remove surgically.

clue.text: A bit of muscle is required to lean forward

parts.note: to tend is to lean or incline
on means forward, as in moving on

explanation.surface: Some muscle strength is needed to bend forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough cord of tissue joining a muscle to bone, part of the muscle system.

clue.text: A right that is followed by left shows spirit

explanation.surface: A political manifesto about right and left reveals a party's spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the airy sprite who serves Prospero in Shakespeare's The Tempest.

clue.text: City once perhaps holding the record

indicators.note: holding means the rearranged word contains the record
perhaps suggests the word once may be arranged another way

parts.note: a log is a written record, such as a ship's log

explanation.surface: A former capital that once held a famous record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ONCE into CONE, and 'holding' puts LOG inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A large city on the Rhine in Germany, also the source of eau de cologne.

clue.text: With this the cook may well prepare fine food

definitions.text: With this the cook may well prepare fine food

parts.words: With this the cook may well prepare fine food
parts.note: fine food here is not haute cuisine but food shredded into small particles, like grated cheese or zest

explanation.surface: A kitchen tool that helps a chef turn out gourmet dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen utensil with a rough perforated surface that shreds cheese or vegetables into fine pieces.

clue.text: A beast turned up carrying papers to be checked

indicators.note: carrying means the turned animal holds the newspapers
in a down entry, turned up means the animal is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a deer is a wild beast
the press means newspapers

explanation.surface: A wild animal appears holding documents that need checking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' makes DEER into REED, and 'carrying' sets PRESS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Repressed means held back or restrained, as feelings are checked.

clue.text: Jack goes off quietly with it

parts.note: milk that goes off turns sour
p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A man named Jack leaves quietly, taking something with him.
explanation.definitionFit: A roasting jack is a device that turns meat on a spit; a turnspit served the same role.

clue.text: Ray's more correct when a girl appears

indicators.note: correct invites us to put the letters right by rearranging them

parts.note: the name and its possessive s give four letters

explanation.surface: Ray is more accurate when a young woman turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'Ray's' counts as a letter here, part of the anagram's eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, also the herb.

clue.text: Cancel it in error and there'll be a song made

indicators.note: something done in error is done wrongly, so these letters are set down in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A clerk cancels an order by mistake, and out of the muddle a song is born.
explanation.definitionFit: A canticle is a hymn or chant taken from the Bible, used in church services.

clue.text: The radio officer's place for relaxation on board

definitions.text: The radio officer's place for relaxation on board

parts.words: The radio officer's place for relaxation on board
parts.note: a ship's radio officer is traditionally nicknamed after the electrical ... of early wireless sets; the clue plays on a leisure spot aboard ship

explanation.surface: Where the ship's radio operator goes to unwind during a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: The ship is S.S. and a recreation area is a PARK, so a park on board the S.S. gives the nickname for the radio operator.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparks is the long-standing nickname for a ship's wireless operator, from the sparking of early transmitters.

clue.text: Some regret only attending one school

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people regret going to just one school.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a famous English public school near Windsor.

clue.text: New post quite undemanding? That's illuminating!

indicators.note: a new version of the word post has its letters rearranged

parts.note: light work is easy, not demanding

explanation.surface: Someone finds their new job very easy and is enlightened by the experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage lamp casts a strong beam on a performer, lighting them up.

clue.text: Medical practitioners exercise back here

indicators.note: back tells us to read the medical officers and the exercise class together from the end

parts.note: MOs are medical officers, doctors in the services
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Doctors are told to take exercise to strengthen their backs.
explanation.walkthrough: MOS + PE reads MOSPE; 'back' turns the whole run. 'Here' is the definition, pointing to the Surrey racecourse town that 17 down also refers to.
explanation.definitionFit: A Surrey town famous for its racecourse and Derby, the place the clue's 'here' points to.

clue.text: Discomfort is of little account to a man

parts.note: a/c is the short form of account
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man shrugs off his pain as unimportant.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull continuing pain is a kind of physical discomfort.

clue.text: A receptacle on certain occasions

indicators.note: to occasion is to cause, so the letters are caused to take a fresh form

explanation.surface: A vessel used only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasions' looks like part of the phrase 'on certain occasions' but is the anagram signal working on ON CERTAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A box, jar or tin, anything that holds something inside.

clue.text: Sit near awkward characters-less agreeable

indicators.note: the letters of the words are put in an awkward, jumbled order

explanation.surface: Being seated next to difficult people makes for an unpleasant time.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative meaning more unpleasant or more spiteful, the opposite of nicer.

clue.text: A Scot, we hear or 13 might attract him

definitions.text: A Scot, we hear or 13 might attract him

parts.words: A Scot, we hear or 13 might attract him
parts.note: 'A Scot' heard aloud is Ascot, a racecourse near Windsor; 13 is Epsom, another course, so both draw a fan of the turf

explanation.surface: A Scottish visitor, or a Surrey town, catches someone's interest.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a Berkshire racecourse; EPSOM, the answer to 13 across, is the Surrey course that runs the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes to horse-race meetings, drawn to famous courses.

clue.text: Make notes about plagiarism when scoring

indicators.note: about means the singing goes round the copying

parts.note: to sing is to make musical notes
a crib is something copied from someone else

explanation.surface: Writing down notes about copying while grading papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make notes' wants to be the definition, but scribing means marking with a pointed tool, scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: To scribe is to mark a line on wood or metal with a pointed tool, scratching it.

clue.text: Climbers make them for cash

parts.note: as can mean for, in the sense of in the role of
cents are small coins, cash

explanation.surface: Mountaineers undertake climbs to raise money.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers going up a mountain make climbs or upward journeys.

clue.text: Sticks up for the self-complacent

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: gums are glues, things that stick

explanation.surface: Someone defends people who are pleased with themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug means irritatingly pleased with oneself, self-satisfied.

clue.text: Leather-but not for show

definitions.meaning: an animal skin used as leather
to keep something out of sight, rather than display it

explanation.surface: An item of leatherwear that is not meant to be displayed.
explanation.definitionFit: One spelling serves as the noun for an animal's tanned skin and the verb meaning to conceal.

clue.text: Fish kept on weed

parts.note: had means kept, held
dock is a broad-leaved weed

explanation.surface: A fish was raised on a diet of pondweed.
explanation.definitionFit: A North Atlantic food fish of the cod family.

clue.text: Beat in a thin plate

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash

explanation.surface: Hammering metal into a thin sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamina is a thin layer, scale or sheet of material.

clue.text: Seeing a little notice in this place, hold on

parts.note: an ad is a small advertisement or notice
here means in this place

explanation.surface: Seeing a small sign nearby, someone waits.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast, holding on tightly.

clue.text: A plant obtainable from North American nurserymen

indicators.note: the run of letters can be obtained from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A plant sold by garden centres in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The genus name for heath and heather, flowering shrubs.

clue.text: Deceitful junior employee?

definitions.meaning: a worker ranked beneath others, as if an ..., the question mark marking the split reading

explanation.surface: A dishonest young member of staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Means sly or dishonest, and split into two words describes a hired hand of lower rank.

clue.text: Bars flighty creatures

definitions.meaning: long bars forming a fence or a track
marsh birds of the genus Rallus, creatures of flight

explanation.surface: Barriers for nervous animals.
explanation.definitionFit: One spelling serves for metal or wooden bars and for a family of wading birds.

clue.text: Tin-ore working in the east

indicators.note: the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Tin ore being mined in eastern lands.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary name for the countries of Asia, the lands to the east.

clue.text: One finds many in easily-managed quarters

indicators.note: in places the thousand and the one inside the word for tame

parts.note: docile means tame and easily managed
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, many
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single person finds lots of people living in comfortable lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal word for one's home, the place where one is lodged or quartered.

clue.text: Storm back, getting in the way, to have a look

indicators.note: getting in says the reversed fury goes inside the road

parts.note: RD is road, a way

indicators.note: back means the word for storm is read backwards

parts.note: to rage is to storm

explanation.surface: A storm rolls back across the road, and someone pauses to look.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at it attentively, gazing or having a look.

clue.text: A clouded picture

parts.note: not a blurred photo but a painting of a sky filled with clouds

explanation.definitionFit: A painting or view of the sky, often full of clouds.
